statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 21% sits in the 20-24 watch band, below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold and eases one point as the overnight low holds. The narrow 13:00Z-15:00Z window spanning the 13:30Z U.S. cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release is the session's identified checkpoint, where opening-auction continuation with a failed first retracement is the named conditional risk. Stress at 79% describes a difficult environment created by the Brent premium above $107 and a 19-year-high 10-year yield rather than by an observed mean-reversion failure.
headline: NQ holds 30,675.25, down 0.69% from settle, with the 30,638.50 overnight low unextended for more than two hours; Brent's extension to $107.46 keeps Stress at 79% while Tail eases to 21% in the watch band
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 30,675.25 in the Monday Globex session, 214.00 points and 0.69% below Friday's 30,889.25 settlement. The week opened at 30,870.00, printed a high of 30,920.75 and ground down to 30,638.50 around 03:00Z. That low is the structural centre of this hour's assessment: it undercut Friday's low, it was rejected, and in the more than two hours since it was set price has not gone back to it, trading at 30,675.25 roughly 37 points above it. Repeated extension after failed retracements is the pathological pattern this contract scores, and its opposite has now been observed twice in succession.

The catalyst backdrop has, if anything, tightened. Brent crude has extended to $107.46, up 3.01%, and WTI to $94.35, up 2.09%, after the U.S. rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and observing a ceasefire. Iran's foreign ministry says no rejection has reached it through official channels and that it is still awaiting a definitive U.S. answer to a seven-day timeline, so the headline risk is live rather than resolved. Brent has travelled from roughly $97 to above $107 during this episode and is up 18.75% on the month. That sits on top of a U.S. Treasury curve at multi-decade highs: the 2-year is 4.87%, the 10-year 5.18% and the 30-year 5.47% on the latest H.15 data, with the 10-year having touched 5.22% on Friday, its highest in about 19 years, on sticky inflation, heavy issuance and expectations of at least one further rate increase this year.

Cross-asset equity confirmation remains incomplete, which is the decisive point. Korea's Kospi fell 2.3% to 6,916.30 with semiconductor names leading, and the Shanghai Composite lost 1.7% to 3,820.82, but the Nikkei 225 was essentially flat at 66,333.53, the Hang Seng rose 0.7% to 24,684.09 and the ASX 200 added 0.3%. Two independent sources agree on that split, and the Nikkei and Hang Seng readings have improved slightly over the past hour rather than deteriorated. E-mini S&P futures at 7,775.75 are down 0.36%, roughly half the Nasdaq-100 decline, framing the move as duration and rate sensitivity concentrated in expensive technology rather than a broad risk-off impulse. The VIX last printed 14.87, down 5.11% on Friday, and no protection bid has appeared since. Friday's cash session closed higher, with the Nasdaq-100 index at 30,608.14, up 0.42% and within 0.5% of its 52-week high, so the overnight move is a give-back from record territory rather than the continuation of an established downtrend.

Tail therefore eases one point to 21%, inside the 20-24 watch band and below the 25% block threshold. An aligned commodity, rates and geopolitical catalyst stack is present and is the reason Tail sits at the top of that band rather than in the low band, but the observed price path is not pathological: the overnight range is 0.91% of settle, a downside probe was rejected and has not been retested for over two hours, implied volatility is at the low end of its range, and Asian equity confirmation is conflicting and marginally improving. Under this contract an aligned catalyst stack without observed persistent one-way structure belongs in Stress, which holds at 79%, at the top of the high band. Confidence rises to 81% on verified current futures, cross-asset, commodity and calendar evidence corroborated by two independent sources for the Asian session, limited by the absence of live overnight volatility and Treasury prints while cash markets are closed and by a shared context file that is stale at over five hours old with its futures and calendar sections unavailable.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held at 6-8% through the Sunday Asian and European hours, drifted to 9-14% across the U.S. afternoon and the Globex reopen as Stress climbed from 56% to 76%, eased to 9-12% between 00:00Z and 02:00Z, then stepped to 21% at 03:00Z when NQ first took out Friday's low and to 22% at 04:00Z. Dominant mode was normal for twenty-two of the twenty-four hours, turning mixed at 02:00Z and trend-down for the final two. Twenty-two hours mapped to EA_ON and the most recent two to WATCH.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 05:00Z hour on 28 September through 04:00Z on 29 September. Tail stays inside the 20-24 watch band for twenty of the twenty-four hours and in the 18-19% low band for the other four, peaking at 23% for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours that contain the 13:30Z U.S. cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release. Those two hours carry the event/whipsaw mode, and their named structural risk is opening-auction continuation with a failed first retracement, a conditional checkpoint rather than observed structure. Tail is lowest at 18% across the 21:00Z-22:00Z CME maintenance break, when no meaningful price discovery is available, and returns to 19-20% through the Tuesday Asian hours, where liquidity is thin but the information set is settled. Stress holds between 73% and 79% throughout, reflecting the Hormuz oil premium and multi-decade-high yields ahead of a week carrying JOLTS, PCE, ISM Manufacturing and payrolls. Confidence peaks at 83% during U.S. cash hours and troughs at 74-76% across the maintenance break and the far edge of the horizon.
